title: The Motion-First Secret
hook: If you are copying and pasting your image prompts into an AI video generator, you are ruining your video before it even starts rendering. Today I'll show you the counterintuitive motion-first secret that fixes this instantly.
cta: Thanks for watching! Subscribe to Sylvester's AI Lab for straightforward, hype-free AI tutorials, and I'll see you in the next video.

sections.heading: The Double-Prompting Trap
sections.voiceover: Most people craft a stunning still image in Midjourney or Flux, then copy that wall of text into Runway or Kling. The result is a chaotic, morphing mess — the AI re-interprets pixels it was already given. This is the double-prompting trap.

sections.heading: The Motion-First Shift
sections.voiceover: Shift to a motion-first mindset. Your text prompt has only two jobs: describe the camera work, and describe how the world behaves. The image already carries the subject.

sections.heading: The Three-Step Formula
sections.voiceover: Step one is Camera Movement — slow pan right, cinematic zoom. Step two is Subject Action — minimal, physically plausible motion. Step three is Environmental Physics — leaves rustle, smoke drifts, dust floats.

sections.heading: A Live Demonstration
sections.voiceover: A bad prompt lists every visual detail and the video model morphs it. The motion-first prompt names only the camera push, the arm raise, and the floating dust — and the result is smooth and consistent.

sections.heading: Real Limitations
sections.voiceover: Be honest: motion-first prompting still struggles with complex high-velocity motion like tying laces or shuffling cards. For that, the industry is moving to motion-transfer from real footage. But for ninety percent of cinematic shots, it is your fastest path to success.

sections.heading: Sylvester's Verdict
sections.voiceover: Adopt the motion-first methodology now for all your image-to-video projects. Skip the generic prompt-engineering guides and focus on the physical mechanics of the camera and the environment.
